How much does it cost to run an electric oven?

A conventional electric oven heats a large box of air, which makes it one of the more expensive ways to cook a small meal.

Cost per use
36p
About £74.73 a year at 1 hour per use, 4 uses a week.

Standing charge not included.

Adjust for yours
Ofgem price cap average for 1 Oct – 31 Dec 2026 (standard variable tariff, Direct Debit, England, Scotland & Wales).

About these figures

A typical electric oven uses about 2,100 watts (1,500–3,500W depending on the model). Used for 1 hour per use, 4 uses a week, it costs about 36p per use and £74.73 a year at the current price cap rate.

Worth knowing: Once hot, the oven switches its element on and off to hold the temperature, so it isn't at full power all the time. We assume full power 65% of the time, including preheat.

Source for the typical figure: CSE 'What uses watt?' table. See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Cook several things at once when the oven is on.
  • Fan ovens can usually run about 20°C lower than conventional settings.
  • Keep the door shut, because each opening loses a lot of heat.

Questions

How much does it cost to run an electric oven per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 2100W model costs about 36p an hour, allowing for it running at full power about 65% of the time.

How much does it cost to run an electric oven per year?

About £74.73 a year, based on 1 hour per use, 4 uses a week. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my electric oven's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
